root_cause.detail: activation.py derives run_id = uuid5(NAMESPACE_URL, f'{ACTIVATION_IDEMPOTENCY_REVISION}:{release.id}:{slot_number}'). release.id is the fixed Window 2 authorized release id 375a88da-da88-5ebf-9daf-cb09934e02b8, so run_id is identical for every Window 2 activation. The Repair #2 attempt (2026-08-29 06:13) persisted research run 71819ef3 (status FAILED, terminal) and terminal coordinator run ad0dd306 with that same run_id. On the Repair #3 resume, activation.py line 208 finds the existing run and line 211 calls authority.authorize(existing, existing_business); the existing run's persisted CrawlPolicy was built from the FULL statement ceilings (max_pages 8, max_total_bytes 2000000) while the current release carries the reduced remaining ceilings (max_logical_requests 6, max_total_bytes 1999128), so authorization.py line 105 raises research_scope_mismatch.
root_cause.even_without_reduced_ceilings: If the envelope had used full ceilings, authorize(existing) would pass and return the FAILED terminal run; production_runtime._m1 then re-reads run.status == FAILED (terminal) and immediately re-raises TruthfulTerminal('M1_RESEARCH_FAILED') WITHOUT executing the fixed robots path. Separately, the terminal coordinator run ad0dd306 already holds one accepted M1 artifact, so execution.py would skip M1 and start at M2. Clearing the stale state is required for the repair to take effect under either ceiling choice.
root_cause.is_this_an_eligible_defect: Arguably yes - 'the deterministic idempotency keys of a repair-resumed run collide with a prior failed attempt's persisted terminal state, preventing the repair from taking effect'. But the corrective action is a targeted data cleanup, not a code change; a code change (detect superseded-release terminal state and re-initialize) would be a heavier Repair #4.
